1x4iaq8.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of uneven road
1x4iaq8.why: The triangle with two close bumps is the uneven road sign (strada deformata): it warns of an irregular, broken or poorly maintained road surface.

1jiy0gn.q: The sign shown can be combined with a maximum speed limit sign
1jiy0gn.why: The uneven road sign can be paired with a maximum speed limit sign to impose a speed suited to the damaged surface.

16c2zse.q: The sign shown indicates a stretch of uneven road 380 metres long
16c2zse.why: The supplementary panel with vertical arrows shows the length of the hazard (estesa): the road is uneven for 380 metres.

jn1045.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with an irregular surface
jn1045.why: The triangle with two close bumps is the uneven road sign (strada deformata): it warns of an irregular, broken or poorly maintained road surface.

7mqojd.q: The sign shown warns of a road in poor condition
7mqojd.why: The triangle with two close bumps is the uneven road sign (strada deformata): it warns of an irregular, broken or poorly maintained road surface.

1nnlvly.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
1nnlvly.why: It is a danger sign (segnale di pericolo): triangular with a red border, it warns of an uneven road.

1w4jn45.q: The sign shown is generally placed 150 metres before a stretch of road with an irregular surface
1w4jn45.why: Like all danger signs, outside built-up areas it is normally placed about 150 metres before the stretch with the irregular surface.

1q62z4w.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of damaged road
1q62z4w.why: The triangle with two close bumps is the uneven road sign (strada deformata): it warns of an irregular, broken or poorly maintained road surface.

e2rb7e.q: The sign shown, if on a yellow background, is used where there are roadworks
e2rb7e.why: Danger signs with a yellow background are used for temporary hazards caused by roadworks (cantieri stradali).

bfphbk.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is important to anticipate possible skidding of vehicles coming from the opposite direction
bfphbk.why: On an uneven surface, oncoming vehicles can also skid and drift into your lane, so you must be ready for it.

1gkffwd.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must adapt your speed to the particular conditions of the road surface
1gkffwd.why: An irregular surface reduces grip and stability, so speed must be adapted to the condition of the road surface.

1mcvexj.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must drive at a moderate speed if towing a trailer
1mcvexj.why: On an uneven road a trailer can bounce and sway easily, so you must drive at a moderate speed.

3q8kk2.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must reduce speed to avoid excessive stress on and damage to the suspension
3q8kk2.why: Bumps in the surface put heavy stress on the suspension (sospensioni): slowing down prevents damage and loss of control.

1bqrefq.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must hold the steering wheel firmly to control possible skidding
1bqrefq.why: The uneven surface can push the vehicle off line, so hold the steering wheel firmly to control any skidding.

urtrsm.q: The sign shown is a prescription sign
urtrsm.why: It is a danger sign, not a prescription sign (segnale di prescrizione): it warns of an uneven road but imposes no obligation or ban.

2raevr.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous descent
2raevr.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); a dangerous descent sign shows a slope with a percentage.

1wzuvgj.q: The sign shown warns of several consecutive bends
1wzuvgj.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); consecutive bends are shown by the double bend sign.

1l85ghz.q: The sign shown warns of a series of humps
1l85ghz.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); a hump is shown by a single central rise.

zaugdd.q: The sign shown warns of a sharp change in the road's gradient
zaugdd.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); changes in gradient are shown by the hump or steep ascent/descent signs.

1ubrska.q: The sign shown warns of a double bend
1ubrska.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); a double bend is shown by an S-shaped arrow.

cwx533.q: The sign shown warns of a hump
cwx533.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); a hump is shown by a single central rise.

lvqzhi.q: The sign shown warns of a dip or a hump
lvqzhi.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); humps and dips have their own signs, with a single rise or a single hollow.

xlpq38.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with limited visibility
xlpq38.why: The sign shows two close bumps and means uneven road (strada deformata); limited visibility is typical of the hump or bend signs.

1ofwkkh.q: The sign shown indicates a stretch of uneven road 320 metres long
1ofwkkh.why: A panel without arrows gives the distance: the uneven road begins in 320 metres. The length of the stretch would be shown with vertical arrows.

1dfeog4.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must drive in the middle of the carriageway
1dfeog4.why: There is no requirement to drive in the middle: keep to the right, slow down and hold the steering wheel firmly.

25egoi.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is not necessary to slow down in poor visibility
25egoi.why: In poor visibility you must always slow down, especially on an uneven surface that can cause skidding.

1p6l8j3.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must watch out for the carriageway narrowing
1p6l8j3.why: The sign concerns an irregular surface, not a narrowing: that has its own road narrows sign (strettoia).

1xz4238.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking is prohibited
1xz4238.why: This danger sign does not ban overtaking: it calls for caution and a suitable speed; a ban needs its own sign.

g9l3ql.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down only if vehicles are coming from the opposite direction
g9l3ql.why: You must always slow down because of the irregular surface, whether or not traffic is coming the other way.

18gxaau.q: The sign shown warns of a hump
18gxaau.why: The triangle with a single rise is the hump sign (dosso): a crest that limits visibility.

1r6gamc.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is dangerous because of limited visibility
1r6gamc.why: The hump hides whatever is beyond the crest, so the stretch is dangerous because of limited visibility.

uitelw.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres before a hump
uitelw.why: Like other danger signs, outside built-up areas it is normally placed 150 metres before the hump.

1xar5ed.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must bear in mind that visibility is limited
1xar5ed.why: You cannot see the road beyond the top of the hump, so visibility is limited.

nde8j2.q: The sign shown warns of an ascent followed by a descent
nde8j2.why: A hump is an ascent followed by a descent, with a crest where visibility is reduced.

1rhxl1i.q: The sign shown warns of a change in the road's gradient with limited visibility
1rhxl1i.why: A hump is a change of gradient (up then down) that reduces visibility.

13621o7.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must reduce speed according to visibility
13621o7.why: Visibility is limited on a hump, so moderate your speed to be able to stop in time.

1t2xi7d.q: Where the sign shown is present, U-turns are prohibited
1t2xi7d.why: Near humps and bends, U-turns (inversione di marcia) are prohibited because of poor visibility.

o81ps9.q: Where the sign shown is present, stopping and parking are prohibited on both the uphill and downhill sections
o81ps9.why: On humps both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are prohibited, uphill and downhill, because a stopped vehicle would not be seen.

10befrt.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking is prohibited on the uphill section if the road is two-way with only two lanes
10befrt.why: On a two-way road with only two lanes, overtaking is banned on the uphill side of a hump because you cannot see oncoming traffic.

yxx96r.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
yxx96r.why: It is a danger sign: a red-bordered triangle warning of a hump.

1gtksqi.q: The sign shown can be used to warn of artificial speed humps
1gtksqi.why: The hump sign can also warn of artificial humps, i.e. speed bumps (dossi artificiali).

1nbz2g5.q: The sign shown warns of a dip
1nbz2g5.why: The sign shows a rise, so it means a hump; a dip (cunetta) has the symbol of a hollow.

qjyprj.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of uneven road
qjyprj.why: The single-rise sign means a hump; an irregular surface is shown by the uneven road sign, with two bumps (strada deformata).

1rhjf4w.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road in poor condition
1rhjf4w.why: The single-rise sign means a hump; an irregular surface is shown by the uneven road sign, with two bumps (strada deformata).

13bycxa.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with an irregular surface
13bycxa.why: The single-rise sign means a hump; an irregular surface is shown by the uneven road sign, with two bumps (strada deformata).

11f1fg.q: The sign shown warns of a bridge
11f1fg.why: The sign means a hump, a crest with limited visibility, not a bridge.

1q6h2r5.q: The sign shown warns of roadworks
1q6h2r5.why: It means a hump; roadworks have their own sign showing a worker (lavori in corso).

tivh82.q: The sign shown warns of the entrance to a tunnel
tivh82.why: It means a hump; a tunnel entrance has its own information sign (galleria).

1snj1op.why: It is a danger sign warning of a hump: it bans no vehicle from passing.

7a1nav.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking is prohibited on the downhill section
7a1nav.why: Overtaking is banned only on the uphill side, where visibility is lacking; on the downhill side visibility returns and overtaking is allowed.

17zjk6i.q: The sign shown is a mandatory sign
17zjk6i.why: It is a danger sign, triangular with a red border; mandatory signs (segnali d'obbligo) are round and blue.

1smo41o.q: Where the sign shown is present, a U-turn may be made on the downhill section
1smo41o.why: On humps, U-turns are prohibited on both the uphill and downhill sections.

1dr1ffv.q: The sign shown is a priority sign
1dr1ffv.why: It is a danger sign warning of a hump; it does not regulate right of way (precedenza).

1lsrpvk.q: The sign shown warns of a dip
1lsrpvk.why: The triangle with a hollow is the dip sign (cunetta): the road goes down and then back up.

1jinwt1.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is dangerous because of a dip
1jinwt1.why: The sign indicates a dip, a hollow that can make the vehicle bounce and collect water.

17dt6rs.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
17dt6rs.why: It is a danger sign: a red-bordered triangle warning of a dip.

1nmtp9u.q: The sign shown is placed before a downhill section followed by an uphill one
1nmtp9u.why: A dip is a downhill stretch followed by an uphill one, the opposite of a hump.

1c4ogn7.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that could flood in heavy rain
1c4ogn7.why: Water collects at the lowest point of the dip, so in heavy rain the stretch can flood.

1bdbsh6.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must reduce speed to avoid damage to the suspension
1bdbsh6.why: Going fast through a dip makes the vehicle bounce and strains the suspension: slow down.

9r2ztq.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must reduce speed to keep control of the vehicle
9r2ztq.why: The bounce in a dip can cost grip and control, so speed must be moderated.

1duomec.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must hold the steering wheel with a firmer grip
1duomec.why: The bounce in the dip can push the vehicle off line, so grip the steering wheel firmly.

15yz8j3.q: Where the sign shown is present and it is raining, you must anticipate that water may collect in the dip
15yz8j3.why: The dip is the lowest point of the road: rain collects there, with a risk of aquaplaning.

mu1pg6.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must anticipate that mud and debris may collect in the dip
mu1pg6.why: Mud and debris carried by water can collect in the hollow and reduce grip.

11pmvjl.q: The sign shown indicates a soft verge
11pmvjl.why: The sign means a dip; a soft verge (banchina cedevole) has its own sign showing a vehicle tilting at the road edge.

1cfiobf.q: The sign shown warns of a soft verge
1cfiobf.why: The sign means a dip; a soft verge (banchina cedevole) has its own sign showing a vehicle tilting at the road edge.

rhr2iu.q: The sign shown warns of an uneven road
rhr2iu.why: The single-hollow sign means a dip; an irregular surface is shown by the two-bump uneven road sign (strada deformata).

15whp6b.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road in poor condition
15whp6b.why: The single-hollow sign means a dip; an irregular surface is shown by the two-bump uneven road sign (strada deformata).

1qavo53.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with an irregular surface
1qavo53.why: The single-hollow sign means a dip; an irregular surface is shown by the two-bump uneven road sign (strada deformata).

1vqokna.q: The sign shown may be placed before an uphill section followed by a descent
1vqokna.why: An ascent followed by a descent is a hump; a dip is the opposite, a descent followed by an ascent.

1i3r5mp.q: The sign shown warns of a narrowing of the carriageway
1i3r5mp.why: It means a dip; a narrowing of the carriageway has the road narrows sign (strettoia).

b350vd.q: The sign shown warns of a hump
b350vd.why: The symbol is a hollow, so it means a dip; a hump (dosso) shows a rise.

xii2of.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down only if vehicles are coming from the opposite direction
xii2of.why: You must always slow down for a dip, regardless of oncoming traffic, to avoid losing control.

fmzphc.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is not necessary to slow down if the dip is visible
fmzphc.why: Even when clearly visible, a dip makes the vehicle bounce and may hold water or mud: always take it slowly.

16ix53w.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking is prohibited if you are driving on a one-way road
16ix53w.why: A dip does not bring an overtaking ban, least of all on a one-way road with no oncoming traffic.

1m40m9r.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous bend to the right
1m40m9r.why: The arrow bending right indicates a dangerous bend to the right (curva pericolosa a destra).

27nfl3.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres from the start of the bend
27nfl3.why: Like other danger signs, outside built-up areas it is normally placed 150 metres before the start of the bend.

gt3lpl.q: The sign shown can be supplemented with a panel reading TORNANTE
gt3lpl.why: If the bend is a hairpin, the sign can carry a TORNANTE (hairpin) panel.

13pe2n8.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is dangerous because of reduced visibility
13pe2n8.why: The bend hides the road beyond it, so visibility is reduced.

4vum4l.q: The sign shown requires you to reduce speed
4vum4l.why: Before a dangerous bend you must reduce speed to take it safely.

1e9n9rt.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous stretch of road
1e9n9rt.why: It is a danger sign warning of a dangerous stretch due to a right-hand bend.

16i05v4.q: Where the sign shown is present, on a two-way road with only two lanes, you must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge
16i05v4.why: On a bend on a two-way, two-lane road, keep as close as possible to the right edge so you do not drift into the other lane.

d7jbnb.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where you must adjust your speed to visibility and the radius of the bend
d7jbnb.why: Speed on a bend must match visibility and the bend radius: the tighter the bend, the slower you go.

xzgrcq.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where the bend must be taken with extra care if the road is wet
xzgrcq.why: On a wet road grip drops and the risk of skidding on a bend rises: take extra care.

1amtt1.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where overtaking is not allowed if the carriageway is two-way with only two lanes
1amtt1.why: The sign warns of a dangerous right-hand curve. On a two-way, two-lane carriageway, overtaking in a curve (curva) is forbidden because visibility is limited.

qezc6l.q: With the sign shown, you must drive at a particularly moderate pace if you are using the space-saver spare wheel (ruotino)
qezc6l.why: A space-saver spare (ruotino) has reduced grip and stability, so in the dangerous curve ahead you must drive very slowly (never above 80 km/h with it in any case).

1obi9tq.q: The sign shown warns of a series of dangerous curves, the first to the right
1obi9tq.why: The sign shows a single dangerous curve to the right. A series of curves uses a different symbol, the double curve (doppia curva), with two bends drawn.

uor7t0.q: The sign shown announces an obligation to turn right
uor7t0.why: This is a danger sign warning of a dangerous right-hand curve. A mandatory turn is shown by a round blue sign with a white arrow.

1rhln9l.q: The sign shown is a regulatory sign
1rhln9l.why: It is a danger sign (red-bordered triangle) warning of a dangerous right-hand curve; it does not impose any prohibition or obligation (prescrizione).

1d6rtyn.q: The sign shown warns of an uphill stretch of road
1d6rtyn.why: The sign warns of a dangerous right-hand curve. A steep climb (salita ripida) has its own sign showing a slope with the gradient percentage.

1hh77il.q: The sign shown announces a lane change
1hh77il.why: The sign warns of a dangerous right-hand curve, not a lane change; lane shifts are shown by specific lane or diversion signs.

by78hq.q: The sign shown warns of a curve to the left
by78hq.why: The symbol bends to the right, so the sign warns of a dangerous curve to the right, not to the left.

isnrl5.q: The sign shown, placed on a two-way road, requires you to move to the left side of the carriageway to take the curve better
isnrl5.why: On a two-way road you must keep as close as possible to the right edge in a curve; moving left risks a head-on collision with oncoming traffic.

1anh7t0.q: The sign shown is normally placed 5 metres before the start of the curve
1anh7t0.why: Like other danger signs, it is normally placed 150 metres before the curve, giving time to slow down.

1290jby.q: The sign shown warns of a two-way, two-lane stretch of road where you may overtake motorcycles without crossing the solid white line
1290jby.why: In a curve on a two-way, two-lane road, overtaking any vehicle is forbidden, motorcycles included.

1igq48y.q: With the sign shown, you must drive as close as possible to the white line separating the two directions of traffic
1igq48y.why: In a curve you must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway, away from the centre line (mezzeria), to avoid oncoming vehicles.

bxzeah.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where stopping is allowed but parking is not
bxzeah.why: Both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are forbidden in a curve, because a stationary vehicle would be hard to see and dangerous.

194z8u6.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where you may overtake motorcycles, even by entering the opposite lane
194z8u6.why: In a curve, with limited visibility, overtaking any vehicle is forbidden and you must never enter the opposite lane.

kxwo82.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where U-turns are allowed
kxwo82.why: U-turns (inversione di marcia) are forbidden in a curve, because poor visibility makes the manoeuvre very dangerous.

i4aewh.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where reversing manoeuvres are allowed
i4aewh.why: Reversing (retromarcia) is forbidden in a curve, because approaching drivers would not see the manoeuvring vehicle in time.

1oghl1f.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where you may overtake motorcycles, even crossing the solid white line slightly
1oghl1f.why: A solid white line must never be crossed, not even slightly, and in a curve overtaking any vehicle is forbidden.

13h4rkc.q: The figure shows a danger sign
13h4rkc.why: A white triangle with a red border is a danger sign (segnale di pericolo); this one warns of a dangerous curve to the left.

1d7j548.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous curve to the left
1d7j548.why: The black symbol bends to the left: this is the dangerous left-hand curve sign (curva pericolosa a sinistra).

1xfsbr1.q: The sign shown warns of a non-straight stretch of road that limits visibility
1xfsbr1.why: A dangerous left-hand curve is a non-straight stretch where visibility is reduced, so it calls for extra caution.

25ldi4.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that curves to the left with limited visibility
25ldi4.why: The sign warns of a dangerous curve to the left, a stretch where the road bends and visibility is limited.

fukxl6.q: The sign shown warns, normally 150 metres ahead, of a dangerous curve
fukxl6.why: Danger signs are normally placed 150 metres before the hazard, in this case a dangerous curve to the left.

o9v43x.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is dangerous due to reduced visibility
o9v43x.why: A dangerous curve hides what lies beyond the bend: reduced visibility is exactly why it is dangerous.

v7z739.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed so that you can stop in case of a sudden obstacle
v7z739.why: Visibility is limited in a curve, so you must slow down enough to stop within the distance you can see if an obstacle suddenly appears.

b8xmep.q: With the sign shown, on a two-way road with only two lanes, you must drive as close as possible to the right edge
b8xmep.why: In a curve on a two-way, two-lane road you must keep as close as possible to the right edge so as not to interfere with oncoming traffic.

1on0h3w.q: With the sign shown, you must adjust your speed according to visibility and the radius of the curve
1on0h3w.why: Speed in a curve must suit visibility and the curve's radius: the tighter the bend and the less you can see, the slower you must go.

1pl7ewt.q: With the sign shown, you must take the curve with more care if the road is wet
1pl7ewt.why: On a wet road tyre grip is lower and the risk of skidding in a curve increases, so more care is needed.

13fladd.q: With the sign shown, you may not overtake other vehicles on a two-way carriageway with only two lanes
13fladd.why: In a curve on a two-way, two-lane carriageway, overtaking is forbidden because visibility is limited and you would have to enter the opposite lane.

5pp59i.q: With the sign shown, you must drive at a particularly moderate pace if you are using the space-saver spare wheel ("ruotino")
5pp59i.why: A space-saver spare (ruotino) has reduced grip and stability, so in a curve you must drive very slowly (never above 80 km/h with it in any case).

1yaf4tf.q: The figure shows a mandatory sign
1yaf4tf.why: It is a danger sign (red-bordered triangle); mandatory signs (segnali di obbligo) are round with a blue background.

jyfkwc.q: The sign shown warns of an obstacle to be passed on the left
jyfkwc.why: The sign warns of a dangerous left-hand curve. 'Pass on the left' is a round blue sign with a diagonal arrow.

1rt15mz.q: The figure shows a no left turn sign
1rt15mz.why: It is a danger sign for a left-hand curve. No left turn is a round red-bordered sign with a crossed-out arrow.

txamf7.q: The sign shown imposes an obligation to keep left
txamf7.why: It is a danger sign warning of a left-hand curve and imposes no obligation; in a curve you should actually keep to the right.

10aczqn.q: The sign shown requires you to drive as close as possible to the centre of the road
10aczqn.why: In a curve you must drive as close as possible to the right edge, not the centre, to avoid oncoming vehicles.

1ymg2j5.q: The sign shown indicates a roundabout
1ymg2j5.why: The sign warns of a dangerous left-hand curve. A roundabout (rotatoria) is shown by a sign with three arrows arranged in a circle.

1a4qt60.q: The figure shows a regulatory sign
1a4qt60.why: It is a danger sign warning of a left-hand curve; it is not a regulatory sign (prescrizione), as it imposes no prohibition or obligation.

e9t9o6.q: The sign shown indicates a diversion due to roadworks
e9t9o6.why: The sign warns of a dangerous left-hand curve. Roadworks diversions use signs with a yellow background.

1xp2ihe.q: With the sign shown, on a one-way road you must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway
1xp2ihe.why: The duty to keep as close as possible to the right edge in a curve applies to two-way roads; on a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic.

1wywycq.q: With the sign shown, stopping is allowed but parking is not
1wywycq.why: Both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are forbidden in a curve, because a stationary vehicle would be hard to see.

aina07.q: With the sign shown, on a two-way, two-lane road, you may overtake motorcycles without entering the opposite lane
aina07.why: In a curve on a two-way, two-lane road, overtaking any vehicle is forbidden, motorcycles included.

18kgsgl.q: With the sign shown, U-turns are allowed
18kgsgl.why: U-turns (inversione di marcia) are forbidden in a curve because of poor visibility.

brgh06.q: With the sign shown, reversing manoeuvres are allowed
brgh06.why: Reversing (retromarcia) is forbidden in a curve, because approaching drivers would not see the manoeuvring vehicle in time.

fympmf.q: With the sign shown, vehicles using the space-saver spare wheel ("ruotino") may not pass
fympmf.why: The sign does not ban anyone: a vehicle on a space-saver spare (ruotino) may pass, but must drive very slowly.

whwadw.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous double curve, the first to the right
whwadw.why: The symbol shows two bends in succession, the first bending right: this is the double curve sign (doppia curva) with the first bend to the right.

7hm4vw.q: The sign shown warns of a non-straight stretch of road that limits visibility
7hm4vw.why: A double curve is a non-straight stretch where visibility is reduced.

1gge6nm.q: The sign shown may be supplemented with a panel reading TORNANTI
1gge6nm.why: The double curve sign can be supplemented with a TORNANTI panel to indicate a series of hairpin bends, typical of mountain roads.

13gdvdw.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed so that you can stop in case of a sudden obstacle
13gdvdw.why: Visibility is limited in the curves, so you must slow down enough to stop within the distance you can see.

1prqt24.q: The sign shown may be supplemented with the panel shown
1prqt24.why: The panel with vertical arrows and 2.8 km gives the length (estesa) of the winding stretch and can supplement the double curve sign.

v8ehc7.q: The figure shows a danger sign
v8ehc7.why: A red-bordered triangle is a danger sign (segnale di pericolo); this one warns of a dangerous double curve, the first to the right.

236uoi.q: The sign shown warns, normally 150 metres ahead, of a dangerous double curve
236uoi.why: Danger signs are normally placed 150 metres before the hazard, in this case a double curve.

1e8831j.q: With the sign shown, you must moderate your speed
1e8831j.why: A dangerous double curve reduces visibility and vehicle stability, so you must slow down.

1njw058.q: On a road with only two lanes and two-way traffic, with the sign shown you must drive as close as possible to the right edge
1njw058.why: In curves on a two-way, two-lane road you must keep as close as possible to the right edge to avoid oncoming vehicles.

i16xqf.q: With the sign shown, you must adjust your speed according to visibility and the radius of the curves
i16xqf.why: Speed must suit visibility and the radius of the curves: tight, blind bends require a lower speed.

1tcrgqw.q: With the sign shown, you must take the curves with more care when it rains
1tcrgqw.why: In the rain grip is lower and the risk of skidding in curves increases, so more care is needed.

1c5b4zk.q: With the sign shown, you must adjust your speed according to the vehicle's load
1c5b4zk.why: A loaded vehicle is less stable and needs more distance to stop, so speed in the curves must also suit the load.

6waqga.q: In the dangerous curves announced by the sign shown, overtaking is forbidden if the carriageway has two lanes and two-way traffic
6waqga.why: In curves on a two-way, two-lane carriageway, overtaking is forbidden because visibility is limited and you would have to enter the opposite lane.

1sv84op.q: On a two-lane, two-way road, with the sign shown you should pay particular attention to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
1sv84op.why: In curves visibility is reduced, and oncoming vehicles can appear suddenly or swing wide.

8fz80e.q: The sign shown warns of a diversion due to roadworks
8fz80e.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. Roadworks diversions use signs with a yellow background.

16pu0rs.q: The sign shown warns of a motorway exit slip road
16pu0rs.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. Motorway exits are shown by green information signs.

j1xcia.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous descent
j1xcia.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. A dangerous descent (discesa pericolosa) has a sign showing a slope with a percentage.

1hugw78.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with a slippery surface
1hugw78.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. A slippery road (strada sdrucciolevole) has a sign showing a skidding car.

oo3fra.q: The sign shown warns of a junction
oo3fra.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. A junction is shown by signs with a cross or a branching road.

14qxs2.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with an uneven surface
14qxs2.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve. An uneven road (strada deformata) has its own sign with a bumpy profile.

k0jyoa.q: The sign with the panel shown warns of a 3.8 km long stretch of road with a series of dangerous curves
k0jyoa.why: A panel without arrows gives the distance: the double curve begins 3.8 km ahead. The length of a stretch (estesa) is shown with vertical arrows beside the number.

5ycleh.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where U-turns are allowed
5ycleh.why: U-turns (inversione di marcia) are forbidden in curves because of poor visibility.

5zc90k.q: With the sign shown, placed on a two-lane, two-way road, overtaking is allowed during daytime
5zc90k.why: The ban on overtaking in curves on a two-way, two-lane road applies at all times, day and night.

1etlagv.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where reversing is allowed
1etlagv.why: Reversing (retromarcia) is forbidden in curves, because approaching drivers would not see the manoeuvring vehicle in time.

18l09q4.q: With the sign shown, you need to keep a moderate speed only in the first curve
18l09q4.why: Speed must stay moderate for the whole stretch, through both curves, not only the first.

fxsh8a.q: With the sign shown, stopping in the curve is allowed
fxsh8a.why: Stopping (fermata) is forbidden in a curve, like parking, because a stationary vehicle would be hard to see.

1z0t6lu.q: With the sign shown, you may overtake motorcycles and mopeds on a two-lane, two-way road
1z0t6lu.why: In curves on a two-way, two-lane road, overtaking any vehicle is forbidden, including motorcycles and mopeds (ciclomotori).

13296ph.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous double curve, the first to the left
13296ph.why: The symbol shows two bends in succession, the first bending left: this is the double curve sign (doppia curva) with the first bend to the left.

14h41at.q: The sign shown warns of a non-straight stretch of road that limits visibility
14h41at.why: A double curve is a non-straight stretch where visibility is reduced.

151dlgw.q: The sign shown warns of hairpin bends if supplemented with the appropriate panel
151dlgw.why: When supplemented with the TORNANTI panel, the double curve sign warns of a series of hairpin bends (tornanti).

pws9k2.q: The figure shows a danger sign
pws9k2.why: A red-bordered triangle is a danger sign (segnale di pericolo); this one warns of a dangerous double curve, the first to the left.

zay0js.q: The sign shown warns, generally 150 m ahead, of a dangerous double curve
zay0js.why: Danger signs are normally placed 150 metres before the hazard, in this case a double curve.

ou1vzs.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed
ou1vzs.why: A dangerous double curve reduces visibility and vehicle stability, so you must slow down.

1jbw5lh.q: With the sign shown, you must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway, on a road with only two lanes and two-way traffic
1jbw5lh.why: In curves on a two-way, two-lane road you must keep as close as possible to the right edge to avoid oncoming vehicles.

1kff1c6.q: With the sign shown, you must adjust your speed according to visibility and the radius of the curves
1kff1c6.why: Speed must suit visibility and the radius of the curves: tight, blind bends require a lower speed.

123a0zt.q: With the sign shown, you must take the curves with more care when it rains
123a0zt.why: In the rain grip is lower and the risk of skidding in curves increases, so more care is needed.

2vrmbt.q: With the sign shown, you must adjust your speed according to the vehicle's load
2vrmbt.why: A loaded vehicle is less stable and needs more distance to stop, so speed in the curves must also suit the load.

1lmd8i6.q: With the sign shown, overtaking is not allowed on roads with only two lanes and two-way traffic
1lmd8i6.why: In curves on a two-way, two-lane road, overtaking is forbidden because visibility is limited and you would have to enter the opposite lane.

40dvxx.q: With the sign shown, you should pay particular attention to vehicles coming from the opposite direction
40dvxx.why: In curves visibility is reduced, and oncoming vehicles can appear suddenly or swing wide.

5aownb.q: The sign shown warns of a merging road from the left
5aownb.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double curve, the first to the left. A merge (confluenza) has a sign showing a side road joining.

1qywnnd.q: The sign shown warns of a road narrowing
1qywnnd.why: The sign shows a DOUBLE BEND (doppia curva), first to the left: it warns of two consecutive dangerous bends. A road narrowing (strettoia) has a different sign showing the road edges converging.

dkbghb.q: The sign shown warns of a slippery stretch of road
dkbghb.why: The sign shows a DOUBLE BEND (doppia curva), first to the left: it warns of two consecutive dangerous bends. A slippery road (strada sdrucciolevole) is shown by a sign with a skidding car.

16y40iw.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with a series of humps
16y40iw.why: The sign shows a DOUBLE BEND (doppia curva), first to the left: it warns of two consecutive dangerous bends. Humps are warned of by the DOSSO or uneven road (strada deformata) signs, not this one.

geoss5.q: The sign shown warns of a diversion due to roadworks
geoss5.why: The sign shows a DOUBLE BEND (doppia curva), first to the left: it warns of two consecutive dangerous bends. Roadwork diversions use yellow-background temporary roadworks signs.

18m5b3i.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of uneven road
18m5b3i.why: The sign shows a DOUBLE BEND (doppia curva), first to the left: it warns of two consecutive dangerous bends. Uneven road (strada deformata) has its own sign showing a bumpy road profile.

w4nlwc.q: Where the sign shown is present, U-turns are permitted
w4nlwc.why: The sign warns of a dangerous double bend with poor visibility, and U-turns (inversione di marcia) are forbidden on bends.

13460ls.q: Where the sign shown is present, on two-lane two-way roads, overtaking a very slow vehicle is permitted
13460ls.why: On bends on a two-lane two-way road, overtaking is forbidden because of poor visibility, even if the vehicle ahead is very slow.

1do336k.q: Where the sign shown is present, reversing is permitted
1do336k.why: Visibility is limited on dangerous bends, so reversing (retromarcia) is forbidden there.

1m0j8kd.q: Where the sign shown is present, a moderate speed must be kept only on the first bend
1m0j8kd.why: The sign warns of two consecutive bends, so speed must be kept moderate along the whole stretch, through both bends.

1iazsfo.q: Where the sign shown is present, stopping briefly on the bends is permitted
1iazsfo.why: Both stopping (fermata) and parking are forbidden on bends, because a stationary vehicle would be hard to see and dangerous.

q4z1yq.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking motorcycles and mopeds is permitted on two-lane two-way roads
q4z1yq.why: On bends on a two-lane two-way road, overtaking any vehicle is forbidden, motorcycles and mopeds included.

1h4i9s7.q: The sign shown warns of a level crossing with barriers or half-barriers
1h4i9s7.why: The sign with the gate is LEVEL CROSSING WITH BARRIERS OR HALF-BARRIERS (passaggio a livello con barriere o semibarriere), normally placed 150 m before the tracks.

1puytck.q: After the sign shown, if there are half-barriers, a device with flashing red lights is installed
1puytck.why: Level crossings with half-barriers (semibarriere) have two alternately flashing red lights that signal closure.

fa1pz5.q: The sign shown warns of a railway crossing protected by barriers or half-barriers, whatever the number of tracks
fa1pz5.why: This sign is used for any level crossing with barriers or half-barriers, regardless of how many tracks there are.

1nlu9gg.q: The sign shown warns of a railway crossing equipped with barriers or half-barriers
1nlu9gg.why: This is the LEVEL CROSSING WITH BARRIERS OR HALF-BARRIERS sign: the railway crossing is protected by barriers.

1nxp2bw.q: After the sign shown, there may be an acoustic device warning that the barriers or half-barriers are closing
1nxp2bw.why: At a level crossing with barriers there may be, besides the red lights, an acoustic device warning that the barriers are closing.

1cgk5kv.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres before the level crossing
1cgk5kv.why: Like other danger signs, the level crossing sign is normally placed 150 m before the hazard.

6t9f7y.q: Where the sign shown is present, speed must be reduced
6t9f7y.why: When approaching a level crossing you must slow down so you can stop if the barriers are closed or closing.

1d7w0uu.q: After the sign shown, if there are barriers, a device with a steady red light is installed
1d7w0uu.why: Level crossings with full barriers (barriere) have a steady red light that comes on while they are closed.

82xnp.q: The picture shows a danger sign
82xnp.why: It is triangular with a red border, so it is a danger sign, warning of a level crossing with barriers.

v6wuro.q: Where the sign shown is present, speed must be reduced so as to be ready to stop if the barriers are closed
v6wuro.why: The sign warns of a level crossing: you must slow down so that you can stop before closed barriers.

1w92hi2.q: Where the sign shown is present, entering the level crossing is not permitted if heavy traffic prevents clearing it
1w92hi2.why: You must not enter a level crossing if traffic prevents you from clearing it, since your vehicle could be stuck on the tracks.

o7eugw.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must stop if the two flashing red lights are on
o7eugw.why: The two flashing red lights signal that the half-barriers are closing or a train is coming, so you must stop.

15966jt.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must stop if the acoustic device warning of the barriers closing is sounding
15966jt.why: The acoustic device warns that the barriers are about to close, so you must stop and not cross.

gzrki.q: Where the sign shown is present, if the vehicle breaks down on the tracks, the driver must take every useful step to avoid accidents
gzrki.why: If the vehicle breaks down on the tracks, the driver must do everything possible to prevent an accident, such as clearing the tracks and warning railway staff or approaching traffic.

qe677u.q: The sign shown warns of a crossing with a tram line
qe677u.why: The sign warns of a level crossing with barriers; a tram line crossing has a sign showing a tram.

1xcr8q.q: The sign shown warns of a dead-end road
1xcr8q.why: The sign warns of a level crossing with barriers; a dead-end road (strada senza uscita) is a rectangular information sign.

c13pd9.q: The sign shown requires you to stop if the red lights near the barriers or half-barriers are off
c13pd9.why: You must stop when the red lights are on (steady or flashing), not when they are off.

n8yg8u.q: The sign shown indicates a compulsory diversion
n8yg8u.why: It is a danger sign warning of a level crossing with barriers, not a mandatory or diversion sign.

1oecfj9.q: The sign shown allows you to drive between one bar and the other if the half-barriers are closed, after checking that no trains are coming
1oecfj9.why: When the half-barriers are closed it is forbidden to drive between them, even if no train seems to be coming.

3k7o3b.q: The sign shown indicates a guarded parking area
3k7o3b.why: It is a danger sign warning of a level crossing with barriers, not a parking area.

1gr5lxj.q: The sign shown is located before the vertical sign DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS
1gr5lxj.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is used at level crossings without barriers; this sign is for level crossings with barriers.

aqrmvf.q: The sign shown warns of fencing barriers around a roadworks site
aqrmvf.why: The gate shown represents level crossing barriers, not fencing around a roadworks site.

1s92vxp.q: The sign shown requires giving way to prison police vehicles leaving prisons
1s92vxp.why: The sign warns of a level crossing with barriers and imposes no duty to give way to police vehicles.

o2yole.q: Where the sign shown is present, parking at or near level crossings is permitted
o2yole.why: Parking, and also stopping, are forbidden at or near level crossings (passaggi a livello).

5gqu1v.q: Where the sign shown is present, you need to slow down only in poor visibility
5gqu1v.why: You must always slow down near a level crossing so you can stop if the barriers close, whatever the visibility.

4299xz.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is possible to cross the tracks if they are blocked by trestles with red and white stripes
4299xz.why: Red-and-white striped trestles (cavalletti) block the way, so you must not cross the tracks.

10b9jzv.q: Where the sign shown is present, stopping is permitted but parking is not near or at the tracks
10b9jzv.why: Near or at level crossings, both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are forbidden.

mcz3k2.q: The sign shown warns of a level railway crossing without barriers
mcz3k2.why: The sign with the steam locomotive is LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS (passaggio a livello senza barriere), normally 150 m before the tracks.

1r281d5.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres from the tracks, supplemented by the relevant distance panel
1r281d5.why: The sign is normally placed 150 m before the tracks, above the distance panel (pannello distanziometrico) with three red bars.

mkd1rl.q: The sign shown requires the utmost caution
mkd1rl.why: A level crossing without barriers is unprotected, so the driver must take the utmost care and check that no train is coming.

1nunu3c.q: The picture shows a danger sign
1nunu3c.why: It is triangular with a red border, so it is a danger sign, warning of a level crossing without barriers.

jdt90l.q: After the sign shown, the ST. ANDREW'S CROSS sign is installed, positioned before the tracks
jdt90l.why: At a level crossing without barriers, the ST. ANDREW'S CROSS (croce di S. Andrea) is placed right next to the tracks.

mnrz2r.q: The sign shown is supplemented by the distance panel with three red bars
mnrz2r.why: Below the sign is the distance panel with three red bars (about 150 m), the first one you meet.

2h7t4o.q: After the sign shown, the DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS sign is installed if the railway line has more than one track
2h7t4o.why: If the railway line has more than one track, the DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is placed next to the tracks.

st7tir.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down according to the visibility of the railway line
st7tir.why: Without barriers the driver must check for trains, so speed must be reduced according to how much of the railway line can be seen.

pi2ecw.q: Where the sign shown is present, the utmost caution must be used
pi2ecw.why: A level crossing without barriers has no protection, so you must proceed with the utmost caution.

d52e8i.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down so as to be able, if necessary, to stop the vehicle before the railway crossing
d52e8i.why: You must slow down so that you can stop before the tracks if a train is coming.

1jj9ew0.q: Where the sign shown is present, before crossing you must make sure no trains are coming from either the right or the left
1jj9ew0.why: Without barriers nothing stops the traffic for you, so before crossing you must look both ways.

xy83l6.q: Where the sign shown is present, parking or stopping near or at the tracks is not permitted
xy83l6.why: Near or at level crossings, both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are forbidden.

fpb3lh.q: The sign shown indicates a crossing with a tram line
fpb3lh.why: The locomotive indicates a railway level crossing without barriers; a tram line crossing has a sign showing a tram.

1o5l6hu.q: The sign shown warns of a level railway crossing equipped with half-barriers
1o5l6hu.why: The locomotive sign means a level crossing without barriers; crossings with barriers or half-barriers use the gate sign.

45x62e.q: The sign shown is placed on the second distance panel with red bars
45x62e.why: The sign is placed above the first distance panel, the one with three red bars, about 150 m from the tracks.

1gz4c2t.q: The sign shown warns of a level crossing with barriers
1gz4c2t.why: The locomotive means a level crossing without barriers; one with barriers uses the gate sign.

1df8bel.q: The sign shown indicates a railway station 150 metres ahead
1df8bel.why: The sign warns of a level crossing without barriers, not a railway station.

16ipti6.q: The sign shown may be supplemented by a panel with the word TRAM
16ipti6.why: The sign concerns trains at a level crossing without barriers; trams have their own tram crossing sign.

1pqycic.q: The picture shows a priority sign
1pqycic.why: The red-bordered triangle with a locomotive is a danger sign, not a priority sign (segnale di precedenza).

m7v1v2.q: Where the sign shown is present, you need to slow down only in fog
m7v1v2.why: You must always slow down according to how well you can see the railway line, not only in fog.

zpep3t.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must stop before the tracks if the light or acoustic signals are not working
zpep3t.why: You must stop if a train is coming or the light or acoustic signals are active; if they are off you cross carefully after checking.

o5uzid.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is possible to cross the tracks if they are blocked by trestles with red and white stripes
o5uzid.why: Red-and-white striped trestles (cavalletti) block the way, so you must not cross the tracks.

9vglp9.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must sound the horn before crossing the tracks
9vglp9.why: There is no requirement to use the horn (clacson); you must slow down and check that no train is coming.

17y1xea.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking by moving into the opposite lane is permitted
17y1xea.why: Overtaking is forbidden near level crossings without barriers.

l35cc9.q: The sign shown indicates that the railway line has only one track
l35cc9.why: The single ST. ANDREW'S CROSS (croce di S. Andrea) indicates a level crossing without barriers with only one track.

12hfye2.q: The sign shown is placed in the immediate vicinity of a railway crossing without barriers
12hfye2.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is placed right next to level crossings without barriers.

1hanh0e.q: The sign shown is placed in the immediate vicinity of the track
1hanh0e.why: Unlike other danger signs, the ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is not 150 m ahead but right next to the track.

pg490c.q: The sign shown is placed on the road after the LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign
pg490c.why: You first meet the LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign at 150 m, then the ST. ANDREW'S CROSS next to the track.

p3x8qe.q: The picture shows a danger sign
p3x8qe.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is classed as a danger sign even though it is not triangular.

8jsni6.q: The sign shown may be placed either horizontally or vertically
8jsni6.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS may be installed with its long side horizontal or vertical, depending on the space available.

1mjugd0.q: The sign shown warns of a railway line with several tracks
1mjugd0.why: The single cross means one track; for more tracks the DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is used.

1x3w5ht.q: The sign shown warns of a junction of four roads
1x3w5ht.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS indicates a single-track level crossing without barriers, not a road junction.

1iy523g.q: The sign shown warns of a single-track tram line
1iy523g.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS concerns railways, not tram lines, which have their own sign.

1om4ff8.q: The sign shown is installed near a level crossing with half-barriers
1om4ff8.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is used only at level crossings without barriers.

b54maf.q: The sign shown is placed before the LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign
b54maf.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS comes after the LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign, right next to the track.

1ce2c.q: The sign shown is supplemented by a green light and a steady red light
1ce2c.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS may be fitted with red lights that flash when a train approaches, not a green light and a steady red light.

19lvzo1.q: The sign shown is normally located 150 metres from the tracks
19lvzo1.why: The ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is placed right next to the track, not 150 m away.

1ui2qnn.q: The sign shown requires you to stop at the stop line if a train is approaching.
1ui2qnn.why: At a level crossing without barriers, if a train is coming you must stop at the stop line (striscia di arresto).

1ct9lel.q: The sign shown is placed in the immediate vicinity of a level railway crossing without barriers
1ct9lel.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is placed next to the tracks at level crossings without barriers with more than one track.

qmtbc4.q: The sign shown indicates that the railway line has more than one track
qmtbc4.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS (doppia croce di S. Andrea) indicates a railway line with two or more tracks.

16agu8z.q: The sign shown warns you to take care before crossing because more than one train could pass
16agu8z.why: With several tracks, after one train passes another may follow, even from the opposite direction.

jcgdui.q: The sign shown is located after the distance panels with red bars
jcgdui.why: The red-bar distance panels come before the crossing; the DOUBLE CROSS stands after them, right next to the tracks.

1v0c65f.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
1v0c65f.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is classed as a danger sign even though it is not triangular.

1ye67ud.q: Sign (A) may be combined with sign (B)
1ye67ud.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS (A) can be combined with a STOP sign (B) where the railway line is poorly visible; you must then always stop.

w7jl1x.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres from the tracks
w7jl1x.why: The DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS is placed right next to the tracks, not 150 m away.

1wak78i.why: The two signs belong to different kinds of level crossing: (B) warns of a crossing with barriers or half-barriers, while the double St Andrew's cross (A) stands next to the tracks at crossings without barriers.

s4m3kw.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous double road junction
s4m3kw.why: This is the double St Andrew's cross (croce di Sant'Andrea doppia): it marks a level crossing without barriers with two or more tracks, not a road junction.

fbjmfi.q: The sign shown indicates that the railway line has only one track
fbjmfi.why: The double cross means a level crossing without barriers with two or more tracks; a single track is shown by the single St Andrew's cross.

a52bd3.q: The sign shown may be placed before a railway crossing with half-barriers
a52bd3.why: The St Andrew's cross is used only at level crossings without barriers or half-barriers (semibarriere); crossings with half-barriers are announced by the triangle showing a gate.

c2glec.q: The sign shown indicates that you may meet two consecutive level crossings less than 150 metres apart
c2glec.why: The double St Andrew's cross marks a single level crossing without barriers that has two or more tracks, not two consecutive crossings.

1sx6m0p.q: The sign may have a yellow background in the case of work on the tracks
1sx6m0p.why: The St Andrew's cross always has a white background with a red border; yellow backgrounds are used for triangular danger signs at roadworks (cantieri).

qbmt1g.q: The panels shown are placed before any type of level crossing
qbmt1g.why: The distance panels (pannelli distanziometrici) are placed before every type of level crossing, with or without barriers.

1rp395k.q: The panels shown are normally placed at about 150, 100 and 50 metres from the railway crossing
1rp395k.why: The three-bar panel stands about 150 m from the level crossing, the two-bar panel about 100 m and the one-bar panel about 50 m.

1nwo8fg.q: The panels shown indicate that you are approaching a level crossing
1nwo8fg.why: The number of red bars decreases as you get closer to the level crossing, showing the remaining distance.

zfsfw1.q: The panel with three red bars (A) is placed below sign (B)
zfsfw1.why: The three-bar panel, at about 150 m, is mounted beneath the 'level crossing with barriers' sign, which is also placed about 150 m before the crossing.

1alxj57.q: In the case of a railway crossing without barriers, panels (A) are placed before sign (B)
1alxj57.why: The distance panels come at 150, 100 and 50 m before the crossing, while the St Andrew's cross (B) stands right next to the tracks.

1hgyebn.q: The panel with three oblique red bars is the first of the panels you encounter when approaching a level crossing
1hgyebn.why: The three-bar panel is at about 150 m and comes first; then the two-bar panel (100 m) and the one-bar panel (50 m).

1kkv6mb.q: The panels shown can be found only if the level crossing has barriers
1kkv6mb.why: The distance panels are placed before any level crossing, including those without barriers.

6fznmf.q: The panels shown are prescription signs
6fznmf.why: These are distance panels belonging to the level-crossing warning signs; they do not impose any obligation or prohibition.

pd7mjo.q: The panels shown indicate roadworks in progress
pd7mjo.why: They show the distance to a level crossing: about 150, 100 and 50 metres.

km2igp.q: The panels shown have as many diagonal bars as the level crossing has tracks
km2igp.why: The number of bars shows the distance to the level crossing (3 = 150 m, 2 = 100 m, 1 = 50 m), not the number of tracks.

vck4op.q: The panels shown, if they have two bars, indicate a railway crossing with only two tracks
vck4op.why: The two-bar panel means the level crossing is about 100 m ahead; it says nothing about the number of tracks.

12zq965.q: The panels shown are installed on trestles that prohibit transit across the railway crossing
12zq965.why: They are fixed panels at the roadside showing the distance to the level crossing; they do not prohibit passage.

t3idl5.q: The sign shown warns you to moderate your speed because a little further ahead you might cross paths with a tram
t3idl5.why: The sign warns of a tram line crossing or running along the road ahead, so you must slow down.

ujs6e4.q: The sign shown, placed outside built-up areas, warns of a tram line not controlled by traffic lights
ujs6e4.why: The tram sign is used for tram lines not controlled by traffic lights, both outside and inside built-up areas.

oiqc40.q: The sign shown, placed in built-up areas, warns of a crossing with a tram line not controlled by traffic lights
oiqc40.why: Inside built-up areas too, the sign warns of a crossing with a tram line not controlled by traffic lights.

1ovgwcz.q: The sign shown warns, both outside and inside built-up areas, of a tram line not controlled by traffic lights
1ovgwcz.why: The sign applies both outside and inside built-up areas for tram lines that are not controlled by traffic lights.

rbfuqt.q: The sign shown warns of a tram line that crosses the carriageway
rbfuqt.why: The sign warns that a tram line crosses the carriageway (carreggiata) ahead.

sii1a9.q: The sign shown warns of a tram line that reduces the space available for vehicle traffic
sii1a9.why: The sign can also warn of a tram line running on the carriageway and reducing the space available for vehicles.

130bwll.q: Where the sign shown is present, the driver must pay greater attention so as not to obstruct the tram
130bwll.why: A tram runs on fixed rails and cannot swerve, so you must take care not to get in its way.

1mwx0ns.q: Where the sign shown is present, the driver must pay greater attention because a tram may cross their path
1mwx0ns.why: The sign warns that a tram may cross your path ahead, so extra attention is needed.

qp6xfc.q: Where the sign shown is present, a moving tram may be overtaken on the right if there is enough space
qp6xfc.why: A moving tram is normally overtaken on the right when there is room; on the left only on one-way streets or when there is no room on the right.

k6goek.q: Where the sign shown is present, you may drive on the tracks provided you do not obstruct the tram
k6goek.why: Driving on the tram tracks is allowed as long as you do not obstruct the tram.

1da68fl.q: Where the sign shown is present, a tram stopped in the middle of the road for passengers to board and alight may be overtaken on the right only if there is a dedicated passenger island
1da68fl.why: A tram stopped mid-road for passengers may be overtaken on the right only if there is a passenger island (salvagente); otherwise you must stop.

ewtvb0.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must watch out for any pedestrians at the tram stop
ewtvb0.why: At tram stops there may be pedestrians boarding, alighting or crossing the road, so you must be careful.

1banzbi.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must be aware that wheel grip may decrease if you brake on the tracks
1banzbi.why: Metal rails, especially when wet, give less grip than asphalt, so braking on the tracks can make the wheels slide.

cg6pb8.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must bear in mind that a tram needs a longer stopping distance than motor vehicles
cg6pb8.why: A tram has steel wheels on rails and a large mass, so it needs a longer distance to stop than a motor vehicle.

1aj9o5p.q: The sign shown warns of possible trolleybus traffic
1aj9o5p.why: The sign shows a tram and warns of a tram line; trolleybuses (filobus) do not run on rails.

bqw4gv.q: The sign shown may be supplemented with a device with two red lights that light up alternately
bqw4gv.why: Two alternating flashing red lights belong to level crossings; the tram sign specifically marks a tram line not controlled by lights.

wf23in.q: The sign shown requires you to give way to trolleybuses
wf23in.why: It is a danger sign warning of a tram line; it does not impose giving way and has nothing to do with trolleybuses.

1h1jyds.q: The sign shown prohibits overtaking trams
1h1jyds.why: A danger sign does not ban overtaking: a tram may be overtaken, normally on the right, when there is enough room.

53g1m2.q: The sign shown warns of a railway level crossing without barriers
53g1m2.why: The sign warns of a tram line; a level crossing without barriers is marked by the St Andrew's cross.

1sa71e4.q: The sign shown warns of an area where only public service vehicles may travel
1sa71e4.why: The sign warns of a tram line and does not restrict traffic to any category of vehicle.

1cmqhfq.q: Where the sign shown is present, you are required to give way to trolleybuses
1cmqhfq.why: The sign concerns tram lines and imposes no duty to give way to trolleybuses (filobus).

mplmgl.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking trams is prohibited only for motorcycles
mplmgl.why: The sign does not prohibit any category of vehicle from overtaking trams.

18e2gav.q: Where the sign shown is present, driving on the tram tracks is prohibited
18e2gav.why: You may drive on the tram tracks as long as you do not obstruct the tram.

100m3vy.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking the tram is allowed only on the left
100m3vy.why: A tram is normally overtaken on the right; overtaking on the left is allowed on one-way streets or when there is no room on the right.

1rq1uzg.q: Where the sign shown is present, overtaking the tram is allowed only on the right
1rq1uzg.why: A tram is normally overtaken on the right, but overtaking on the left is also allowed on one-way streets or when there is no room on the right.

1p5tdxh.q: Where the sign shown is present, a tram stopped for passengers to board and alight may be overtaken on the right when there is no passenger island
1p5tdxh.why: Without a passenger island (salvagente) you must stop behind the tram while passengers get on and off; overtaking on the right is allowed only where there is an island.

18be5a2.q: The sign shown warns of a bus parking area
18be5a2.why: The sign shows a tram and warns of a tram line, not a bus parking area.

uek0j4.q: The sign shown warns of a lane reserved for trolleybuses
uek0j4.why: The sign warns of a tram line; reserved lanes are shown with information signs and road markings.

629lfq.q: The sign shown warns of a pedestrian crossing
629lfq.why: This is the 'pedestrian crossing' danger sign (attraversamento pedonale), warning of zebra stripes ahead.

13m9kd6.q: Where the sign shown is present, the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing on the stripes
13m9kd6.why: At zebra crossings drivers must give way to pedestrians who are crossing or about to cross.

19a9uyg.q: On extra-urban roads the sign shown is normally placed 150 metres from the crossing
19a9uyg.why: Like all danger signs, outside built-up areas it is normally placed 150 m before the hazard; in towns the distance can be shorter.

1poj20w.q: The sign shown may also be placed in built-up areas
1poj20w.why: The sign is used both outside and inside built-up areas, where it may be placed less than 150 m from the crossing.

1h9cpwl.q: The sign shown implies a ban on overtaking a vehicle that has stopped to let pedestrians cross
1h9cpwl.why: It is forbidden to overtake a vehicle that has stopped or slowed at a pedestrian crossing to let pedestrians cross.

11929qw.q: Where the sign shown is present, you may not overtake vehicles slowing down to let pedestrians cross
11929qw.why: The Highway Code forbids overtaking vehicles that slow down or stop to let pedestrians cross on the stripes.

1a0mazl.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down so as to be ready to stop if pedestrians are crossing the carriageway
1a0mazl.why: When approaching the stripes you must slow down and be ready to stop to give way to pedestrians.

6g59mr.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must take care not to run into the back of vehicles stopping to give way to pedestrians
6g59mr.why: Vehicles ahead may stop suddenly to let pedestrians cross, so you must keep a safe following distance.

cewb4m.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must not park or stop on the pedestrian stripes
cewb4m.why: Both parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) are prohibited on pedestrian crossings.

ebiqf2.q: Where the sign shown is present, failing to give way to pedestrians crossing on the zebra stripes results in a deduction of points from the licence
ebiqf2.why: Failing to give way to pedestrians on the stripes brings a fine and the loss of 8 points from the licence.

oybq3v.q: The sign shown warns of a place frequented by children
oybq3v.why: Places frequented by children have the 'children' sign (bambini) with two running figures; this one marks a pedestrian crossing.

1i993ab.q: The sign shown warns of a pedestrian avenue
1i993ab.why: The sign warns of a pedestrian crossing with stripes, not a pedestrian-only avenue.

w23nrx.q: The sign shown requires you to use the horn to make pedestrians move
w23nrx.why: You must give way to crossing pedestrians; using the horn to make them move is not required and is wrong.

fs6bx.q: The sign shown allows vehicles to stop on the pedestrian crossing, provided there is enough room left for pedestrians
fs6bx.why: Stopping and parking on a pedestrian crossing are always prohibited.

jkafdk.q: The sign shown prohibits pedestrian access
jkafdk.why: It is a danger sign warning of a pedestrian crossing; the ban on pedestrians is a different, round sign.

1p41exl.q: The sign shown warns of a pedestrian zone
1p41exl.why: A pedestrian zone (area pedonale) has a blue rectangular sign; this triangle warns of a pedestrian crossing.

w603iz.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is compulsory to sound the horn if pedestrians are crossing on the zebra stripes
w603iz.why: When pedestrians are on the stripes you must stop and give way, not sound the horn.

vkbl5.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down only if there are children crossing on the zebra stripes
vkbl5.why: You must slow down and be ready to stop for any pedestrian crossing, not only children.

1uydf0m.q: Where the sign shown is present, pedestrians must give way to vehicles
1uydf0m.why: On zebra crossings it is drivers who must give way to pedestrians who are crossing.

1mpacy1.q: Where the sign shown is present, it is not compulsory to give way to pedestrians crossing on the zebra stripes
1mpacy1.why: Giving way to pedestrians on zebra stripes is compulsory; failing to do so costs 8 licence points.

r234ps.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must give way only to pedestrians crossing from the left
r234ps.why: You must give way to all pedestrians crossing on the stripes, from whichever side they come.

80lzwy.q: The sign shown warns of a pedestrian overpass
80lzwy.why: The sign warns of an at-grade zebra crossing; with an overpass pedestrians would not cross the carriageway at all.

1f9rusc.q: The sign shown warns of a pedestrian underpass
1f9rusc.why: The sign warns of a zebra crossing on the carriageway, not a pedestrian underpass (sottopasso).

isc7k6.q: The sign shown is placed at the pedestrian crossing itself
isc7k6.why: As a danger sign it is placed before the crossing, normally 150 m outside built-up areas; at the crossing itself the blue square sign is used.

1rbq2z7.q: The sign shown warns of a cycle crossing
1rbq2z7.why: This is the 'cycle crossing' danger sign (attraversamento ciclabile), warning of a point where cyclists cross the road.

dgreai.q: The sign shown is a danger sign
dgreai.why: It is a triangle with a red border, the typical shape of danger signs.

16v3dfu.q: The sign shown warns of a crossing for cyclists, marked by the appropriate markings on the carriageway
16v3dfu.why: The cycle crossing is marked on the carriageway with dedicated stripes, and this sign warns of it in advance.

o3vsxe.q: The sign shown warns that you are approaching a place from which cyclists may come
o3vsxe.why: The sign warns that ahead cyclists may enter or cross the road.

ujwq31.q: The sign shown is normally placed 150 metres before the cycle crossing
ujwq31.why: Like other danger signs, it is normally placed 150 m before the hazard; in built-up areas the distance may be shorter.

cmci9k.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed so as not to endanger the safety of cyclists
cmci9k.why: The sign calls for caution: you must reduce speed so as not to endanger crossing cyclists.

1dmu8jr.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must behave in such a way as not to endanger or obstruct cyclists
1dmu8jr.why: Near a cycle crossing you must drive so as not to endanger or obstruct cyclists.

p3g6dk.q: Where the sign shown is present, you must slow down and be ready to stop, if necessary, to give way to crossing cyclists
p3g6dk.why: At cycle crossings drivers must give way to cyclists, so you must slow down and be ready to stop.

1yhiuk2.q: Where the sign shown is present, you may not overtake vehicles that have stopped to let cyclists cross the carriageway
1yhiuk2.why: It is forbidden to overtake vehicles that have stopped or are slowing to let cyclists cross.

1w0azi9.q: The sign shown is placed at the cycle crossing itself
1w0azi9.why: Being a danger sign, it is placed before the cycle crossing, normally 150 m ahead of it.

1mr3rl6.q: The sign shown is a prescription sign
1mr3rl6.why: It is a triangular danger sign: it warns of a cycle crossing but does not impose obligations or bans.

f1x93k.q: The sign shown prohibits cyclists from passing
f1x93k.why: The sign warns of a cycle crossing; the ban on bicycles is a round sign with a red border.

n5xait.q: The sign shown marks the start of a cycle path
n5xait.why: The start of a cycle path (pista ciclabile) is shown by a round blue sign with a bicycle; this triangle warns of a cycle crossing.

mhleum.q: The sign shown indicates that a cycle race is taking place
mhleum.why: This danger sign warns of a cycle crossing (attraversamento ciclabile) or a stretch where cyclists often enter or cross the road; it does not mean a cycle race is under way.

ip24gi.q: The sign shown indicates an area reserved for moped traffic
ip24gi.why: This danger sign warns of a cycle crossing (attraversamento ciclabile) or a stretch where cyclists often enter or cross the road; it has nothing to do with mopeds or areas reserved for them.

d7pfg5.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must sound the horn if there are cyclists crossing on the stripes
d7pfg5.why: Cyclists using the cycle crossing must be let through by slowing down and stopping if needed; sounding the horn is not required and can startle them.

z8wr5h.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must bear in mind that cyclists must give way to vehicles
z8wr5h.why: At a cycle crossing it is drivers who must give way to cyclists who are crossing, not the other way round.

4krui5.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must give way only to cyclists crossing from the right
4krui5.why: At a cycle crossing you must give way to crossing cyclists coming from either side, left as well as right.

1mfxtj9.q: The sign shown is placed before a dangerous descent
1mfxtj9.why: The triangle with a downhill profile and 10% is the dangerous descent sign (discesa pericolosa), placed about 150 m before the slope.

6v3n3o.q: The sign shown warns of a particularly dangerous descent
6v3n3o.why: The sign warns of a dangerous descent (discesa pericolosa) with a 10% gradient, a steep stretch that calls for extra caution.

2g45wr.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road on which the vehicle's braking distance increases
2g45wr.why: Going downhill, gravity pushes the vehicle forward, so braking distance is longer than on level road.

1l2prb8.q: The sign shown warns of a descent and specifies its gradient
1l2prb8.why: The sign warns of a dangerous descent, and the figure 10% gives its gradient (pendenza).

3hnazn.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed
3hnazn.why: On a steep descent speed builds up and braking distance grows, so you must moderate your speed.

1n5k23o.q: The sign shown requires you to engage a suitably low gear
1n5k23o.why: On a steep descent you should engage a low gear to use engine braking (freno motore) instead of overusing the brakes.

5smuyk.q: In the presence of the sign shown, engaging a low gear makes it possible to make proper use of engine braking
5smuyk.why: In a low gear the engine holds the vehicle back (freno motore), reducing the need to use the brakes on the descent.

p5nsa8.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must moderate your speed to avoid running into the back of slower vehicles
p5nsa8.why: Downhill, braking distance increases, so moderating speed also helps you avoid rear-ending slower vehicles such as heavy lorries.

1luh7o2.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must avoid prolonged use of the brakes so as not to overheat them
1luh7o2.why: Prolonged braking on a descent overheats the brakes and reduces their effectiveness (brake fade); use a low gear and engine braking instead.

1ki2l2k.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must avoid excessive use of the brakes and control your speed by engaging a low gear
1ki2l2k.why: On the descent, control your speed with a low gear (engine braking) and avoid overusing the brakes, which could overheat.

sypyzv.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must be very careful if the road is wet
sypyzv.why: On a wet road grip is reduced and on a descent braking distance grows even further, so great care is needed.

1eic1pl.q: The sign shown warns of an ascent to be driven in a suitably low gear
1eic1pl.why: The sign warns of a dangerous descent (discesa pericolosa) with a 10% gradient: the black profile slopes down to the right, so it is not an ascent.

22y48w.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous stretch of road due to an uneven surface
22y48w.why: The sign warns of a dangerous descent (discesa pericolosa) with a 10% gradient; an uneven surface has its own sign, uneven road (strada deformata).

17luq2t.q: The sign shown specifies the gradient of an ascent
17luq2t.why: The 10% is the gradient of a descent, not an ascent: the black profile slopes down to the right.

lwv375.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is best driven with the clutch pedal pressed down
lwv375.why: You must not coast downhill with the clutch pressed, as you lose engine braking; keep a low gear engaged.

6kflw6.q: The sign shown warns of a dangerous ascent
6kflw6.why: The sign warns of a dangerous descent (discesa pericolosa) with a 10% gradient; a steep ascent has its own sign with the profile rising to the right.

1weqvu1.q: The sign shown indicates that exceeding a speed of 10 km/h is not permitted
1weqvu1.why: The 10% is the gradient of the descent, not a speed limit; speed limits are shown on circular signs.

ghbwqs.q: In the presence of the sign shown, the danger is lower in case of rain
ghbwqs.why: In rain grip is reduced and braking distance on the descent increases, so the danger is greater.

1tf15pf.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must slow down by continuously using the brakes so as not to damage the gearbox
1tf15pf.why: Continuous braking on a descent overheats the brakes; slow down using a low gear, which does not damage the gearbox (cambio).

kav10h.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must engage the highest gear and adjust your speed with the brakes
kav10h.why: On a steep descent you engage a low gear to use engine braking and avoid overusing the brakes.

106shxa.q: In the presence of the sign shown, you must drive with the clutch pressed down
106shxa.why: Driving downhill with the clutch pressed cancels engine braking and lets speed build up; keep a low gear engaged.

vo625s.q: In the presence of the sign shown, the driver must reduce the safety distance from the vehicle in front
vo625s.why: Downhill, braking distance increases, so the safety distance (distanza di sicurezza) from the vehicle ahead must be increased, not reduced.

pmiv8.q: The sign shown is placed before a steep ascent
pmiv8.why: The sign warns of a steep ascent (salita ripida) with a 10% gradient, placed about 150 m before it.

lwq2h5.q: The sign shown warns of an ascent to be driven with caution
lwq2h5.why: The sign warns of a steep ascent (salita ripida) with a 10% gradient: visibility may be limited and heavy vehicles move slowly, so caution is needed.

1vmhvf5.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road to be driven in a suitably low gear
1vmhvf5.why: A steep ascent should be driven in a suitably low gear, which gives more pulling power.

kkiykt.q: The sign shown specifies the gradient of the ascent
kkiykt.why: The sign warns of a steep ascent, and the figure 10% gives its gradient (pendenza).

1kkpi6d.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road to be driven with the clutch pedal pressed down
1kkpi6d.why: On an ascent you should drive with a low gear engaged; keeping the clutch pressed removes traction and wears the clutch.

jgyj6j.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road in which the vehicle's braking distance increases
jgyj6j.why: Uphill, gravity helps slow the vehicle, so braking distance decreases; it is on a descent that it increases.

npavrl.q: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road that is dangerous because of sharp bends
npavrl.why: The sign warns of a steep ascent (salita ripida) with a 10% gradient; dangerous bends have their own signs.

a2wjcx.q: The sign shown warns of a descent and specifies its gradient
a2wjcx.why: The sign warns of a steep ascent, not a descent: the black profile rises to the right and 10% is the gradient of the climb.

opeo3g.q: The sign shown warns of a narrowing of the carriageway
opeo3g.why: The sign warns of a road narrowing on both sides (strettoia simmetrica).

1lbxlvr.q: The sign shown warns of a narrow passage with likely difficulty in passing oncoming vehicles
1lbxlvr.why: The sign warns of a road narrowing on both sides (strettoia simmetrica): the reduced width can make it hard to pass oncoming vehicles.

1em1udv.q: The sign shown warns of a narrowing on both sides of the carriageway
1em1udv.why: Both lines in the symbol bend inward, so the carriageway narrows on both sides.

1pxu8p0.q: The sign in the figure is a danger sign
1pxu8p0.why: A triangular shape with a red border identifies danger signs (segnali di pericolo); this one warns of a road narrowing.

sj146j.q: After sign (A) you may find sign (B)
sj146j.why: After the narrowing (A) you may find the round sign (B), give way to oncoming traffic, which requires you to let oncoming vehicles through the narrow section first.

1ylhq9c.q: After sign (A) you may find sign (B)
1ylhq9c.why: After the narrowing (A) you may find the blue square sign (B), priority over oncoming traffic, which gives you the right of way through the narrow section.

1tsjxi2.q: The sign shown, if on a yellow background, is placed where roadworks reduce the width of the carriageway
1tsjxi2.why: With a yellow background the sign marks a temporary hazard linked to roadworks, here a work site (cantiere) that narrows the carriageway.

pkb741.q: The sign shown requires you to moderate your speed
pkb741.why: At a narrowing the carriageway gets tighter, so you must slow down and be ready to stop if vehicles come the other way.

1x7guya.q: The sign shown warns of alternating one-way traffic with the obligation to give way to vehicles coming from the other direction
1x7guya.why: The sign only warns of a narrowing and sets no priority; the duty to give way in alternating one-way traffic comes from a specific round sign.

11756bo.q: The sign shown warns that vehicles coming from the other direction must give way to us
11756bo.why: The sign only warns of a narrowing and assigns no priority; right of way over oncoming traffic is shown by the blue square sign.

1ok7sf9.q: The sign shown announces a ban on buses
1ok7sf9.why: The sign warns of a road narrowing on both sides (strettoia simmetrica); transit bans are shown on round red-bordered signs.
